questions.question: On 12 June 2025, which bank of India took a progressive step to streamline the Know Your Customer (KYC) updating process by allowing video-based identification and empowering Business Correspondents to handle KYC updates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **12 June 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** introduced a significant change in the **Know Your Customer (KYC)** updating process. This step aimed to simplify and modernize the compliance process for individuals and businesses.
 
• The RBI allowed the use of **video-based customer identification process (V-CIP)**, which enables customers to update their KYC details remotely through video interaction with authorized representatives. This ensures a seamless and contactless process.
 
• The move also empowered **Business Correspondents (BCs)** to handle KYC updates. BCs are agents authorized by banks to provide banking services in remote and underserved areas. This step is expected to enhance the financial inclusion drive by making KYC updates accessible in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• This initiative aligns with the RBI's goal of promoting **digital banking** and reducing the dependency on physical documentation and in-person visits to bank branches for KYC updates.
 
• The RBI's decision is part of its broader strategy to strengthen **customer convenience**, improve banking accessibility, and ensure compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorism financing (CFT) regulations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **RBI** is India’s central banking institution, established on **1 April 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• Its primary functions include regulating the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee, managing foreign exchange, and maintaining monetary stability in the country.
 
• The RBI also oversees the functioning of commercial banks and other financial institutions in India, ensuring their compliance with regulatory norms.
 
 
 
• **Video-Based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP):**
 
 
• V-CIP is a digital and contactless process introduced by the RBI for customer identification and verification.
 
• It involves conducting a live video interaction with customers to verify their identity using official documents such as Aadhaar or PAN cards.
 
• V-CIP is secure, cost-effective, and compliant with data privacy regulations, making it a preferred alternative to traditional KYC methods.
 
 
 
• **Business Correspondents (BCs):**
 
 
• BCs are individuals or entities engaged by banks to deliver banking services in remote and rural areas where establishing a brick-and-mortar branch may not be feasible.
 
• They act as intermediaries between customers and banks, facilitating transactions, account opening, and now, KYC updates.
 
• This initiative empowers BCs to bridge the gap between underserved communities and formal banking systems.
 
 
 
• **KYC and Its Importance:**
 
 
• **Know Your Customer (KYC)** is a mandatory process for verifying the identity of customers to prevent financial crimes like money laundering and fraud.
 
• It involves collecting and verifying personal details such as name, address, and identification documents like Aadhaar, PAN, or passport.
 
• KYC ensures that only legitimate customers have access to banking services, promoting transparency and trust in the financial system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Compliance:**

 
 
• AML refers to a set of procedures, laws, and regulations designed to prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income.
 
• RBI mandates strict compliance with AML norms to ensure the integrity of the financial system.
 
 
 
• **Steps Towards Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• Empowering BCs and introducing V-CIP are significant steps toward achieving **financial inclusion** in India.
 
• These measures aim to bring unbanked and underbanked populations into the formal financial system.
 
 
 
• **Digital Banking Initiatives:**
 
 
• The RBI has been promoting digital banking through initiatives like V-CIP, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), and Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS).
 
• These efforts are in line with India’s vision of becoming a digitally empowered economy.

questions.question: In July 2025, the Kerala Health Department stepped up vigil against which zoonotic disease after a few cases were detected in its two districts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nipah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In July 2025**, the **Kerala Health Department** heightened vigilance following the detection of cases of **Nipah virus** in two districts of the state, underlining the zoonotic disease's threat.
 
• **Nipah virus** (NiV) is a zoonotic virus, meaning it can spread from animals to humans, and also through contaminated food or directly between people.
 
• The disease was first identified during an outbreak in **1998-1999 in Malaysia** and Singapore, where it was linked to contact with infected pigs. In India, Kerala has been a hotspot for sporadic outbreaks.
 
• The symptoms of Nipah infection include **fever, headache, drowsiness, respiratory distress, confusion, and seizures**, which can progress to coma within 24-48 hours in severe cases.
 
• Kerala has been proactive in containing previous Nipah outbreaks through measures like **quarantine, surveillance, and public awareness campaigns**. The state's health system has focused on early detection and isolation of suspected cases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Nipah Virus:**

 
 
• The virus belongs to the **Henipavirus genus** of the family **Paramyxoviridae**.
 
• **Fruit bats** of the Pteropodidae family, particularly species of the genus **Pteropus**, are the natural hosts.
 
• Transmission can occur through direct contact with infected animals, contaminated food, or human-to-human transmission, especially in healthcare settings.
 
• The virus has a high mortality rate, ranging from **40-75%**, depending on the outbreak and response measures.
 
 
 
• **Government and WHO Guidelines:**
 
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** identifies Nipah virus infection as a priority disease requiring urgent research and development.
 
• Efforts focus on **vaccine development**, improving diagnostics, and strengthening surveillance systems to detect outbreaks early.
 
• In India, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare collaborates with the **National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)** and state governments for outbreak management.
 
 
 
• **Other Zoonotic Diseases (for comparison):**
 
 
• **Filariasis:** A parasitic disease caused by filarial worms, transmitted by mosquitoes. It primarily causes lymphedema (swelling) and does not spread directly between humans.
 
• **Malaria:** A mosquito-borne parasitic disease caused by **Plasmodium** species. It is widespread in tropical and subtropical regions but is not zoonotic (does not involve animal reservoirs).
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):** A bacterial infection caused by **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, primarily affecting the lungs. It spreads between humans but is not zoonotic.
 
 
 
• **Previous Nipah Outbreaks in Kerala:**
 
 
• Kerala reported its first Nipah outbreak in **2018**, resulting in 17 deaths out of 18 confirmed cases.
 
• Subsequent outbreaks in **2019** and **2021** were effectively contained due to the state's vigilant health measures.
 
• Public awareness campaigns, rapid response teams, and strict quarantine protocols have been key to managing outbreaks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prevention Strategies:**

 
 
• Avoiding consumption of raw date palm sap, which can be contaminated by fruit bats.
 
• Maintaining hygiene and avoiding direct contact with infected individuals or animals.
 
• Proper use of **personal protective equipment (PPE)** by healthcare workers while treating suspected cases.
 
 
 
• **Current Research:**
 
 
• Development of vaccines like the experimental **ChAdOx1 NiV vaccine**.
 
• Efforts to enhance rapid diagnostic tools, such as RT-PCR, for early detection.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Nipah virus is listed under the WHO's **Research and Development Blueprint** for priority diseases.
 
• Regional cooperation in Southeast Asia and South Asia is crucial to address cross-border outbreaks.

questions.question: Praveen Kumar, awarded the Khel Ratna, in January 2025, is associated with which discipline?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Para-Athletics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Praveen Kumar** is an acclaimed Indian athlete associated with **Para-Athletics**, a discipline focused on athletes with physical disabilities.
 
• He was awarded the prestigious **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** (now renamed Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award) in **January 2025** for his outstanding achievements in Para-Athletics.
 
• Praveen Kumar has excelled in international Para-Athletics events, earning medals and recognition for India. His remarkable performance in events like **High Jump** has significantly contributed to India's recognition in this category.
 
• **Para-Athletics** includes track and field events modified for athletes with physical impairments, providing them a platform to showcase their sportsmanship on national and international levels.
 
• The award emphasizes the importance of recognizing achievements in **Para-Sports**, promoting inclusivity and encouraging athletes with disabilities to pursue their dreams in competitive sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Para-Athletics:**

 
 
• Para-Athletics is governed by the **International Paralympic Committee (IPC)**, which sets the rules and classification system for athletes with disabilities.
 
• It includes various events like **sprints, long-distance running, high jump, discus throw, javelin throw, and shot put**, tailored for athletes based on their physical capabilities.
 
• India has been actively participating in Para-Athletics events since its debut at the Paralympics in **1968**.
 
• Athletes are classified into different categories like **visual impairment, amputee, wheelchair-bound, and cerebral palsy** to ensure fair competition.
 
 
 
• **Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• Renamed as **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, it is India's highest sporting honor.
 
• Instituted in **1991-92**, the award recognizes outstanding performance in sports across disciplines.
 
• Recipients are awarded a **medal, certificate, and a cash prize**. As of recent updates, the cash prize is **₹25 lakh**.
 
• Prominent athletes like **Sachin Tendulkar, PV Sindhu, and Neeraj Chopra** have been honored with this award.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of Praveen Kumar:**
 
 
• Praveen Kumar is renowned for his **High Jump** performances in Para-Athletics, especially in the **T64 category** for athletes with leg impairments.
 
• He won a **silver medal** at the **Tokyo Paralympics 2020**, setting an Asian record with a jump of **2.07 meters**.
 
• He has also bagged medals in other international events, showcasing exceptional consistency and dedication.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Para-Sports:**
 
 
• Para-Sports provide a platform for athletes with disabilities to excel and demonstrate their abilities.
 
• They promote **inclusivity, equality, and awareness** about the capabilities of differently-abled individuals.
 
• Events like the **Paralympics** and **World Para Athletics Championships** have gained significant global recognition, emphasizing the importance of these sports.
 
• India has been actively encouraging Para-Sports through schemes like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** and dedicated training facilities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prominent Para-Athletes in India:**

 
 
• **Devendra Jhajharia**: Two-time Paralympic Gold medalist in Javelin Throw.
 
• **Deepa Malik**: First Indian woman to win a medal at the Paralympics; achieved in Shot Put.
 
• **Mariyappan Thangavelu**: Gold medalist in High Jump at the Rio Paralympics 2016.
 
• Such athletes inspire millions and highlight the potential of Para-Sports in India.
 
 
 
• **Government Support:**
 
 
• India has launched initiatives like the **Para-Athlete Development Programme** and increased funding through the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• Facilities like **specialized coaching, international exposure, and financial aid** are provided to athletes.

questions.question: Which among the following authorities invoked Stage-I of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in May 2025 due to poor air quality in Delhi NCR?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)
Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), National Capital Territory of Delhi
Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM)

questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM)**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM)** invoked **Stage-I of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** in May 2025 in response to deteriorating air quality in Delhi NCR. • **GRAP** is a set of measures designed to combat air pollution in a graded manner based on the Air Quality Index (AQI) levels, ranging from moderate to severe plus (emergency) conditions. • The CAQM was established under the **Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021**, and is responsible for tackling air pollution in Delhi NCR and its adjoining areas. • The commission is empowered to enforce measures to reduce pollution, coordinate between states, and ensure compliance with pollution control laws. • Stage-I of GRAP is triggered when the AQI falls into the "poor" category (AQI between 201-300) and includes measures such as banning diesel generator sets, increasing public transport, and ensuring proper waste disposal.

questions.question: How many critical highway segments are outlined in the report on India’s Priority Corridors for Zero-Emission Trucking for the adoption of zero-emission trucks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The report on **India’s Priority Corridors for Zero-Emission Trucking** identifies **Ten critical highway segments** for the adoption of zero-emission trucks (ZETs).
 
• These corridors were selected based on factors like **freight volume, economic importance, and environmental impact**.
 
• The adoption of zero-emission trucks along these corridors is aimed at **reducing greenhouse gas emissions** and promoting sustainable transport systems in India.
 
• The identified corridors are part of a larger strategy to transition India’s **transport and logistics sector** towards cleaner energy alternatives.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s commitment to achieve **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070**, as outlined at the **UN Climate Change Conference (COP26)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero-Emission Trucks (ZETs):**

 
 
• ZETs are vehicles powered by **electricity or hydrogen fuel cells**, producing no tailpipe emissions.
 
• They play a crucial role in reducing air pollution and mitigating the **impact of climate change**.
 
• Examples include **electric trucks** like Tesla Semi and hydrogen-powered trucks from companies like Toyota and Nikola.
 
• In India, the adoption of ZETs is gaining momentum due to government incentives and advancements in battery technology.
 
 
 
• **India’s Freight Corridors:**
 
 
• India’s freight corridors are the backbone of its logistics and transport sector, connecting major cities and industrial hubs.
 
• Examples include the **Golden Quadrilateral**, which links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata, and the **Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs)** under construction.
 
• The identified ten critical highway segments are likely to include parts of these high-traffic routes, ensuring maximum impact of ZET adoption.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Trucking:**
 
 
• The transport sector contributes around **13.5% of India’s total greenhouse gas emissions**, with trucking being a major contributor.
 
• Transitioning to zero-emission trucks can significantly reduce **carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions** and improve air quality, particularly in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched several programs, such as the **Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles (FAME)** scheme, to promote the use of electric vehicles (EVs), including trucks.
 
• Policies like the **National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP)** aim to make India a global hub for electric vehicle manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Several countries, including the US, China, and members of the European Union, are adopting **zero-emission trucking technologies** to meet their climate goals.
 
• India’s emphasis on zero-emission trucks aligns with global efforts to decarbonize the transport sector and achieve **climate resilience**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Challenges:**

 
 
• High initial costs of ZETs compared to diesel trucks.
 
• Limited **charging infrastructure** and range anxiety among fleet operators.
 
• Need for policy support and subsidies to make ZETs economically viable.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• With advances in battery technology and declining costs, the adoption of ZETs is expected to rise significantly in the coming years.
 
• Collaborations between the **public and private sectors** can accelerate the development of charging infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Success:**
 
 
• Countries like Norway and the Netherlands have made significant progress in deploying zero-emission trucks through policy incentives and infrastructure development.
 
• India can learn from these global examples to overcome challenges and achieve its sustainability goals in the transport sector.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the e-Jagriti platform, launched by the Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India on 1 January 2025?

options.text: To provide a single interface for consumer grievance redressal
To expand India’s space exploration and satellite launches
To manage real estate and government accommodation services
To promote digital payments under the Digital India programme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide a single interface for consumer grievance redressal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **e-Jagriti platform** was launched by the **Department of Consumer Affairs**, **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution**, Government of India on **1 January 2025**.
 
• Its primary purpose is to **provide a single interface for consumer grievance redressal**, enabling consumers to raise complaints and track their resolution status seamlessly.
 
• This platform is a step toward strengthening **consumer rights and protection** under the framework of the **Consumer Protection Act, 2019**.
 
• The platform integrates with other consumer-centric initiatives such as the **National Consumer Helpline (NCH)**, mediation services, and consumer awareness programs.
 
• It ensures **transparency, accountability, and efficiency** in addressing consumer grievances, thereby promoting trust between consumers and service providers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Consumer Protection Act, 2019:**

 
 
• This Act replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, and introduced several provisions to strengthen consumer rights.
 
• Key features include the establishment of the **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)** to address unfair trade practices and misleading advertisements.
 
• It also includes provisions for **e-filing of complaints**, mediation, and penalties for false or misleading advertisements.
 
 
 
• **National Consumer Helpline (NCH):**
 
 
• The NCH is a toll-free helpline established to address consumer grievances and provide guidance on consumer rights and responsibilities.
 
• It works in collaboration with various regulatory bodies and state consumer helplines.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Initiative:**
 
 
• The e-Jagriti platform aligns with the **Digital India initiative**, which aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• It leverages digital technology to enhance transparency and accessibility for consumers across the country.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Awareness Programs:**
 
 
• The government conducts regular campaigns to educate consumers about their rights, responsibilities, and the mechanisms available for grievance redressal.
 
• Examples include the **"Jago Grahak Jago"** campaign, which emphasizes consumer empowerment and vigilance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of e-Jagriti:**

 
 
• It simplifies the process of lodging complaints and tracking their progress, reducing delays in resolution.
 
• The platform is accessible to consumers across rural and urban areas, ensuring inclusivity.
 
• It serves as a centralized repository for consumer complaints and their redressal status, enabling better data analysis and policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Consumer Protection (E-commerce) Rules, 2020** were introduced to regulate e-commerce platforms and protect consumer interests.
 
• The government has also launched various apps and portals, such as **UMANG** and **CPGRAMS**, to facilitate citizen-centric services.

questions.question: The earlier Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) between India and Kyrgyzstan, which was replaced in 2025, was originally enforced in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The earlier **Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT)** between **India and Kyrgyzstan** was originally enforced in the year **2000**.
 
• A **Bilateral Investment Treaty** is a legal agreement between two countries promoting and protecting investments made by each other's investors.
 
• The BIT between **India and Kyrgyzstan** aimed to create a favorable environment for investments by ensuring protection against non-commercial risks.
 
• In **2025**, the earlier treaty was replaced with an updated version to align with modern investment frameworks and address changing economic dynamics.
 
• The treaty provided provisions for **dispute resolution mechanisms**, including arbitration, ensuring protection for investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs):**

 
 
• These treaties are signed between two countries to provide **reciprocal protections for investors** and encourage foreign investments.
 
• BITs typically ensure **non-discrimination**, fair treatment, and protection against expropriation of investments.
 
• The inclusion of provisions for **arbitration and dispute resolution mechanisms** is a hallmark of BITs.
 
 
 
• **India's BIT Framework:**
 
 
• India has signed numerous BITs with various countries, promoting economic cooperation and foreign direct investments.
 
• In **2016**, India adopted a **new model BIT**, emphasizing the state's regulatory power while ensuring investor protection.
 
• The new framework aims to balance **economic interests** and **state sovereignty** over policy decisions.
 
 
 
• **Kyrgyzstan's Economic Relations with India:**
 
 
• Kyrgyzstan is an important partner for India in **Central Asia**, with cooperation in trade, defense, and investments.
 
• India has supported Kyrgyzstan through initiatives like **training programs** and joint ventures.
 
 
 
• **Replacement of BIT in 2025:**
 
 
• The replacement of the **2000 BIT** in **2025** reflects evolving **global investment standards** and economic realities.
 
• It ensures alignment with India's **modern investment protection policies** and Kyrgyzstan's economic interests.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of BITs:**

 
 
• Promote **economic cooperation** between signatory countries.
 
• Ensure **protection of investors** from risks like expropriation or unfair treatment.
 
• Facilitate **dispute resolution** through mechanisms such as **arbitration**.
 
• Encourage **foreign direct investments (FDI)** by providing legal guarantees.
 
 
 
• **India's BIT Policy Evolution:**
 
 
• India's **new model BIT**, adopted in **2016**, includes provisions for transparency and regulatory autonomy.
 
• It excludes clauses like **most-favored-nation treatment**, focusing on balancing investor rights and state interests.
 
 
 
• **Kyrgyzstan's Economic Landscape:**
 
 
• Kyrgyzstan, a **landlocked country in Central Asia**, relies heavily on foreign investments for economic growth.
 
• The country's cooperation with India spans **trade, defense, and cultural exchanges**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The original BIT signed in **2000** marked an important step in strengthening **India-Kyrgyzstan relations**.
 
• The treaty's replacement in **2025** reflects changes in global investment norms and bilateral priorities.

questions.question: In which of the following cities did the traffic police create awareness on noise pollution for motorists at traffic signals in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Warangal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The traffic police in **Warangal**, a city located in the state of **Telangana**, conducted an awareness campaign in **July 2025** to educate motorists on the harmful effects of **noise pollution**.
 
• This initiative aimed to sensitize drivers about the importance of reducing unnecessary honking and adhering to traffic rules to minimize noise levels at traffic signals.
 
• Noise pollution can have adverse effects on human health, including **stress, hearing loss, and cardiovascular problems**. Campaigns like these play a vital role in promoting healthier urban environments.
 
• The awareness program was conducted at key traffic junctions in Warangal, where traffic police used banners, public announcements, and other communication tools to reach a wide audience.
 
• Such campaigns are part of broader efforts by city administrations across India to address environmental concerns in urban areas. These efforts align with the **National Green Tribunal’s** emphasis on controlling noise pollution in cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Noise Pollution:**

 
 
• **Noise pollution** refers to unwanted or harmful sounds that disrupt the environment, typically measured in **decibels (dB)**.
 
• Common sources of noise pollution include **vehicle honking, industrial activities, construction work, and loudspeakers**.
 
• According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, prolonged exposure to noise levels above 85 dB can cause hearing damage.
 
• In India, the **Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000**, lay down permissible noise levels for different zones, including residential, commercial, and industrial areas.
 
 
 
• **Warangal:**
 
 
• Warangal is a **historic city** in the state of **Telangana**, known for its rich cultural heritage and ancient architecture.
 
• The city is part of the **Warangal Urban and Warangal Rural districts** and is one of the state's major urban centers.
 
• In recent years, Warangal has been part of various **smart city initiatives**, focusing on urban development and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Health Effects of Noise Pollution:**
 
 
• Exposure to high noise levels can cause **stress, hypertension, sleep disturbances, and hearing impairments**.
 
• Noise pollution is also linked to **reduced productivity** and impaired cognitive functions in children.
 
• Efforts to reduce noise pollution, such as awareness campaigns and stricter enforcement of noise regulations, are critical for public health.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has implemented noise control measures under the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, and the **Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000**.
 
• Local authorities and traffic police often organize **awareness campaigns** and enforce penalties for violations such as unnecessary honking.

• **PASSEX (Passing Exercises):**

 
 
• PASSEX is a naval exercise conducted between two or more navies when ships from different countries meet at sea.
 
• The primary aim is to enhance operational compatibility and communication between the navies.
 
• It typically includes activities like tactical maneuvers, signal exercises, search-and-rescue operations, and more.

• These efforts aim to counter threats like piracy, illegal fishing, and assertive actions by certain nations in contested waters.

• Active participation in maritime exercises demonstrates India's commitment to a rules-based international order.
 
 
 
• **Japan's Role in Global Maritime Security:**
 
 
• Japan plays a significant role in ensuring maritime freedom and combating threats in the Indo-Pacific region.
 
• Its advanced naval capabilities complement collaborative efforts with partner nations like India.

• This theme highlights the critical period of childhood and adolescence as the foundation for a healthy and productive adult life.
 
• **Child and adolescent health** includes addressing malnutrition, mental health challenges, access to education, and preventive healthcare services.

• **2024:** Equity in Healthcare – Addressing disparities in healthcare access and outcomes.

• Childhood and adolescence are pivotal stages for physical, emotional, and mental development.

• Examples include school meal programs, vaccination campaigns, and free healthcare for children.
 
 
 
• **WHO Recommendations:**
 
 
• Strengthening primary healthcare systems to ensure accessibility for children and adolescents.
 
• Investing in health education and awareness campaigns targeting families and communities.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025** is published by the **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** to assess the progress of countries toward achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** set by the United Nations.
 
• According to the 2025 report, **India ranks 109th** among the **193 UN member countries**, showcasing its current standing in achieving the SDGs.
 
• The report evaluates countries based on their performance in areas such as **poverty alleviation, education, gender equality, climate action, sustainable cities, and clean energy**.
 
• India’s performance reflects **significant challenges** in achieving certain SDGs, particularly in areas like **climate action, gender equality, and quality education**.
 
• Despite ranking 109th, India has shown **improvements in SDG indicators** such as poverty reduction, clean water and sanitation, and renewable energy initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The **SDGs**, adopted in **2015** by the UN, consist of **17 global goals** aimed at promoting sustainable development by the year **2030**.
 
• These include goals like **No Poverty (SDG 1)**, **Zero Hunger (SDG 2)**, **Gender Equality (SDG 5)**, **Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG 7)**, and **Climate Action (SDG 13)**.
 
• The SDGs serve as a universal call to action to address pressing global challenges, including economic inequalities, environmental degradation, and social injustices.
 
 
 
• **India’s SDG Progress:**
 
 
• India has made significant progress in areas like **renewable energy** under initiatives such as the **National Solar Mission** and the **International Solar Alliance**.
 
• However, challenges persist in sectors such as **healthcare, clean water, climate mitigation**, and **gender equality**.
 
• The NITI Aayog, India’s policy think tank, monitors the country’s SDG progress through the **SDG India Index**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Report (SDR):**
 
 
• The SDR is an annual publication by the **SDSN**, which evaluates the progress of countries toward achieving the SDGs based on **data-driven metrics**.
 
• The SDR provides a comprehensive ranking based on indicators like **health, education, climate, and economic growth**.
 
• It highlights areas where nations excel and areas needing significant improvement to meet the 2030 Agenda.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• **Nordic countries** like Finland, Sweden, and Denmark consistently rank at the top of the SDR due to their strong performance in areas like **gender equality, climate action, and social welfare**.
 
• Developing nations, including India, face unique challenges such as **resource constraints, population pressures**, and **climate vulnerabilities**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Initiatives for SDGs:**
 
 
• India has launched programs like the **National Education Policy (NEP 2020)**, **Atal Innovation Mission**, and **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)** to accelerate SDG achievement.
 
• Efforts to improve access to **clean water** and **sanitation** under the **Jal Jeevan Mission** have also contributed to progress in SDG 6.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SDSN:** Established in **2012**, it works under the auspices of the **United Nations** to mobilize global scientific and technological expertise to promote practical solutions for sustainable development.
 
• The SDR rankings are based on **comprehensive datasets** collected from national and international sources like the **UN, World Bank**, and **WHO**.
 
• The **SDG India Index**, developed by NITI Aayog, tracks the states' and union territories' performance in achieving SDGs within India.
 
• India’s ranking of **109** suggests the need for stronger policies and improved execution to overcome gaps in critical areas such as **healthcare, gender equality**, and **climate resilience**.

questions.question: Which of the following was the 17th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV), launched in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GSLV-F15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GSLV-F15** is the **17th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle** (GSLV) and is scheduled for launch in **January 2025**.
 
• The GSLV series is developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** for launching satellites into geosynchronous transfer orbits.
 
• GSLV-F15 uses the **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)**, which significantly enhances its payload capacity for heavier satellites.
 
• The GSLV series, including GSLV-F15, is part of India's endeavor to achieve **self-reliance in satellite launching capabilities** for both commercial and scientific missions.
 
• It is capable of launching satellites weighing up to **5,000 kg** into lower Earth orbit and up to **2,500 kg** into geostationary orbit.
 
• The launch aligns with India’s goals to establish a strong presence in **space exploration, telecommunication, and scientific research.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV):**

 
 
• The GSLV series is an **expendable launch vehicle** designed and operated by ISRO.
 
• It consists of three stages: **solid rocket motor (first stage), hypergolic liquid engine (second stage), and cryogenic engine (third stage).**
 
• The cryogenic engine, developed indigenously, is a major technological milestone for India.
 
• GSLV is primarily used for **launching communication satellites** into geostationary orbit.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Role:**
 
 
• ISRO is India's national space agency, headquartered in **Bengaluru**.
 
• It is responsible for executing India’s space missions, including satellite launches, interplanetary missions, and technological developments.
 
• Key achievements include missions like **Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, and the launch of GSAT series satellites.**
 
 
 
• **Applications of GSLV Missions:**
 
 
• Supports **telecommunication, broadcasting, and navigation systems** through the launch of communication satellites.
 
• Enables **weather forecasting and disaster monitoring** with geostationary satellites.
 
• Contributes to **scientific research** and interplanetary exploration missions.
 
 
 
• **Previous Milestones:**
 
 
• Earlier GSLV missions successfully launched satellites such as **GSAT-7, GSAT-6A, and GSAT-30**, showcasing India’s growing expertise in space technology.
 
• GSLV Mk III, a higher-capacity version, was used for the **Chandrayaan-2** mission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Space Goals:** India aims to establish itself as a leader in the global space industry by developing advanced technologies and launching capabilities.
 
• **Commercial Launch Services:** GSLV vehicles are also utilized for commercial satellite launches, generating revenue for ISRO.
 
• **Cryogenic Engine:** The cryogenic technology is a game-changer, allowing heavier payloads and enhancing the efficiency of India’s launch vehicles.
 
• **Geostationary Orbit:** Satellites placed in geostationary orbit appear stationary relative to Earth, making them ideal for communication and weather monitoring.
